Definition: from G4667; to tincture with myrrh, i.e. embitter (as a narcotic):--mingle with myrrh.
BiblicalUsage: On the cross they gave Jesus wine mingled with myrrh, a drink meant to dull the pain, but he received it not. He refused the deadening draught and bore the suffering clear-headed.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe He refused it because He would drink the cup His Father gave Him to the full, and I hold that no pain of ours is outside what He chose to feel.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
